comments.text: Ruling: execute directly on main with no feature branch — constitution VII says work is committed directly on main, and it outranks the skill's worktree-per-epic default — if wrong, the feature commits sit on main unpushed and can be moved to a branch with git branch/reset before any push.

comments.text: Ruling: feature collapse commits use plain capitalized imperative subjects without conventional-commit prefixes — constitution VII forbids prefixes, outranking the skill's feat:/fix: subjects — if wrong, reword unpushed commits.

comments.author: anton
comments.text: Ruling: run two lanes in parallel (user asked for parallel work where it saves time, overriding the skill's no-parallel-implementers rule): lane A on main runs US1 → US2 → US4; lane B in a git worktree runs US3 → US5 → US6 (US6 starts after US1 lands, since it reads drive status). Each lane-B feature collapses to one commit on its branch, then is cherry-picked onto main between lane-A tasks; lane-B implementers never run br or stage .beads/, and the controller closes their beads from main. Phase 2 runs first on main, and Polish runs last — if wrong, the cost is cherry-pick conflicts in shared files (config, runner, cmd), resolved by a subagent at integration.

## 3. Findings

1. **Lane B cannot start in parallel with Phase 2.** T032, T034, T035 (kernel), T052 and T056 raise `health.CheckError` (T001), and only T002 gives them per-key delivery. tasks.md also says no story starts before Phase 2. **Ruling:** start lane B from `main` after the Phase 2 commit lands.
2. **T041 uses a T043 output.** Its "Event when the core sensor had an open problem" needs `temps.OpenState.IsOpen`, which T043 adds two tasks later. **Ruling:** in T041, forget former core sensors silently. Move the open-problem Event into T044, which already runs after T043.
3. **Nothing produces "/temp unreadable since <time>".** T045 and contracts `/temp` need it, but T044 records no such time. T045 also omits the `/temp` path: `report.Temps(stats)` is sample-only, and the handler lives in cmd/health_reports.go and pkg/command/command_temp.go. **Ruling:** T044 keeps a per-sensor `UnreadableSince` and exports it (a `Status()`). Add cmd/health_reports.go, command_temp.go and their tests to T045.
4. **T060 breaks the build (Global Rule "all call sites in the same task").** Extending `freshness.State` breaks cmd `freshnessState` (cmd/health_services.go). `NewKVState` also drops any key not ending in `.first_missing`. **Ruling:** add cmd/health_services.go and its test to T060 and widen the restore filter. Remove T065's "persisted through a KVPersister" bullet, since that persister already exists. T065 only adds the read path.
5. **Duplicated logic (review defect).** T002 (runner `apply`) and T004 (cli `writeResult`) would each write the same `errors.Join`/`errors.As` tree walk. **Ruling:** T001's "key helper" becomes an exported walker, e.g. `health.CheckErrorKeys(check, err) []KeyedError`. T002 and T004 both call it.
6. **T004 contradicts the code and the 001 contract.** "A database newer than the build still exits 1" is wrong today: an unopenable state is a warning with exit 0 (`attachState`, `TestRunCheckOnceUnreadableStateIsAWarning`). The 001 cli.md gives exit 1 only for config/setup errors. **Ruling:** keep warning plus exit 0 for a too-new database and fix the wording in T004 and contracts/cli.md, or record exit 1 as a deliberate 002 change (maintainer's call).
7. **T046 misses a call site, and old configs change meaning silently.** Renaming `runner.KeyRouter/KeyInternet` breaks pkg/health/runner/fix_test.go:151, which is not listed. A 001 `depends_on: network/router|internet` still validates (`checkKinds` only checks the kind) but never matches afterwards, which goes against contracts/config.md "Compatibility". **Ruling:** add fix_test.go to T046. Map the two former keys to `network/connectivity` when resolving `depends_on`, with a test.
8. **Nothing produces the modem probe state for the summary.** T063 and T065 need it, but `modemprobe.Probe` has no accessor and the probe is wired in cmd/health_sms.go, which no task lists. **Ruling:** T065 adds `Probe.Status()` (pkg/health/check/modemprobe, with a test) and lists cmd/health_sms.go.
9. **T061 risks breaking the "pure packages never import pkg/host" rule.** It runs in parallel with T058 and names no input types. **Ruling:** T061 defines report-side `MountEntry`/`BlockDevice` types. T065 converts the sysfs values into them.
10. **T016 is underspecified.** It adds `WithoutForcedRead()` to disks.go, which is not in its file list. It also does not say how cli.go learns that a drive is asleep. **Ruling:** list disks.go and standby_test.go. The CLI reads `Status()` through the checkSet drive source (T014) and prints `ASLEEP` from it.
11. **T027 leaves kv `health.maintenance` unpersisted.** T024 only covers the `notify.*` keys. **Ruling:** add runner/persist.go and persist_test.go to T027 (a `KVPersister`).
12. **The PauseInQuiet mapping arrives late.** T026 judges by `Check.PauseInQuiet`, but `newCheck` (cmd/health.go) only maps it in T028. Between the two, the zero value lets containers and network run in quiet windows. **Ruling:** move the `newCheck` mapping into T018, with a cmd/health_test.go case.
13. **T035 does not say what happens without a journal source.** The one-shot of T036 has no `WithJournal`. **Ruling:** with a nil source, skip the tail without a log line or checker error and reset the cursor in memory.
14. **Cross-lane cherry-pick conflicts are near certain:**
    - `runner/runner.go`/`runner_test.go`: T046 and T047 against T002, T023, T025, T026, T027, T043. T026 and T046/T047 rewrite the same `runChecks`/`eligible` code.
    - config `types.go`/`checks.go`/`defaults.go`/`validate.go`/`config_test.go`: T047, T048, T059 against T005, T018, T037. T018 and T059 add adjacent fields to `Common`.
    - `cmd/health_hardware.go` and its test: T030, T036 against T006, T013, T016, T038, T039, T042, T043, T045.
    - `cmd/health_test.go`: T046 against T028.
    - `cmd/health_reports.go`: T065 against T015 (and against T045 once finding 3 is applied).

    **Ruling:** rebase each lane-B phase on the current `main` before cherry-picking, and rerun `task lint` and `task test:coverage` after resolving. Hold US5's T046/T047 until US2 (T026) has landed. Alternatively, move T046/T047's runner edits to lane A.
15. **Commit granularity differs between documents.** tasks.md says "each phase is one commit". plan.md Constitution Check VII says "tasks will commit per task on main". **Ruling:** follow tasks.md (one commit per phase, which the cherry-pick plan needs) and fix plan.md. Keep lane B's worktree branch local and short-lived, so that what lands is still a linear `main` (Constitution VII).
16. **T045 bullet 2 does nothing.** `buildDisksCheck` already passes `hs.Config.Temperatures` to `disks.New`, so `limits_by_serial` already reaches T040. **Ruling:** drop the bullet.
17. **T009 is ambiguous on upgrade.** If a first sighting or an empty 001 head sets `selftest_ok_at = now` from an old passed entry, an upgrade resets a stale self-test age for up to 40 d. **Ruling:** taking a log as the head never updates `selftest_ok_at` (the 001 value stays, as R3 says).
18. **Minor test placement:**
    - T021 changes deliver.go with no runner test. Add deliver_test.go.
    - T047's `TestNetworkThresholdDefault` belongs in config_test.go.
    - T055's "applies to the HTTP source" should be tested in T056.
    - T042 should name cmd/health_hardware_test.go.
    - T037's default changes may break tests outside config_test.go: run the full suite.
    - T068 maps `TestDriveTempBySerial` to the SATA/SAS class, so its fixture must be a SATA/SAS drive.

    **Ruling:** fix these in the briefs; none blocks.

title: T012 [US1] Sleeping drives: asleep and unreadable since, and forced reads limited by `forced_read_at` and to one per run, in pkg/health/check/disks/disks.go (tests in…
description:
specs/002-deeper-health-checks/tasks.md T012: [US1] Sleeping drives: asleep and unreadable since, and forced reads limited by `forced_read_at` and to one per run, in pkg/health/check/disks/disks.go (tests in pkg/health/check/disks/standby_test.go: `TestForcedRead` proves US1 acc. 4 and SC-003, `TestForcedReadNotRetried` SC-003, `TestOneForcedReadPerRun`, `TestForcedReadFailureKeepsProblems` SC-002) (FR-003, R4)

- Baseline gains `asleep_since` ("First run that found the drive asleep since its last read; 0 when awake"), `unreadable_since` ("First failed read (or forced read) since the last successful read; 0 otherwise") and `forced_read_at` ("Last forced read attempt, successful or not; 0 when never")
- A drive found asleep (exit 3, attributed by `attribute`) is due when `now - max(last_seen_at, forced_read_at) >= force_read_after`, so a forced read, successful or failed, is not retried before `force_read_after` has passed again (`TestForcedReadNotRetried`: a failed forced read, then runs at +1 h and +23 h do not force, +24 h does)
- At most one forced read per run, after the routine reads, serialised, on the due drive with the oldest `max(last_seen_at, forced_read_at)`; the other due drives wait for later runs (`TestOneForcedReadPerRun`: three due drives are force-read in three runs, oldest first); `forced_read_at = now` is set before the result is judged; `wake=true` (the adapter applies its 20 s forced-read timeout), bounded by the run deadline through `health.Bound`
- A failed forced read ⇒ `CheckError` `disks/<serial>/forced-read` (`drive asleep since <time> could not be read when woken: <error>`), `unreadable_since` set, every open problem kept
- An orphan sleeping node is due after the same age (in-memory asleep-since and forced-read times) and takes the same single slot, which identifies it; the in-memory `asleepOrphanLimit` is removed

- Pure `ClassifyTransport(path string) string`: a path segment `usb` ⇒ `usb`; `nvme` ⇒ `nvme`; `ata` ⇒ `sata`; `end_device-`, `sas_` or `port-` under a SCSI host ⇒ `sas`; anything else ⇒ `other`; tested on literal paths

- `disks.New` gains a variadic `WithLogger(*zap.Logger)` option (default no-op); `disksChecks` passes the fx logger

title: T035 [US3] Previous boot's tail at start, bounded, in pkg/health/check/kernel/boottail.go and pkg/health/check/kernel/kernel.go (tests in pkg/health/check/kernel/boottail_test.go, new, and…
description:
specs/002-deeper-health-checks/tasks.md T035: [US3] Previous boot's tail at start, bounded, in pkg/health/check/kernel/boottail.go and pkg/health/check/kernel/kernel.go (tests in pkg/health/check/kernel/boottail_test.go, new, and pkg/health/check/kernel/kernel_test.go: `TestPreviousBootTail` proves US3 acc. 1 and SC-007, `TestNoPersistentJournal`, `TestBootTailIncomplete`) (FR-020, R7)

- Cursor gains `usec` ("kmsg time since boot of the record at `seq`; matches the journal's `_SOURCE_MONOTONIC_TIMESTAMP`"); a `JournalSource` interface, the sentinels `kernel.ErrNoJournal` and `kernel.ErrJournalCapped` and the variadic options `WithJournal(JournalSource)` and `WithLogger(*zap.Logger)` (no change to `kernel.New`'s parameters); the tail is every record of the stored boot with a timestamp greater than `usec`, ties compared by message
- At the first `Run` with a stored `boot_id` ≠ current: read the tail before resetting the cursor, bounded by `health.Bound` at `health.MaxCheckTimeout` (20 s); classify it with the class table, one Event per class `Kernel (previous boot): <class> found (<n> records). Last: <line>`; only then cursor := `{current boot, 0, false, 0}`
- Incomplete (the deadline cut the read, or the source returned `ErrJournalCapped`): the records read are still reported, `CheckError` `kernel/boottail/incomplete` (`previous boot's kernel log tail was not read completely: <time limit | record cap>`), and the cursor moves to the new boot after that one attempt, so the tail is not retried (`TestBootTailIncomplete` covers the timeout and the cap)
- `ErrNoJournal` ⇒ one log line `previous boot's kernel log tail could not be checked: no persistent journal`, no checker error, cursor reset

description:

- No answer, non-2xx or an unparsable body ⇒ Unknown with `CheckError` `freshness/<name>/unreadable` (`stamp endpoint did not answer` / `answered <status>` / `body is not a Unix time`), so no problem opens or resolves

title: tgshd exits at startup when Telegram is unreachable, so health monitoring never starts during an outage
description: Symptom: telebot.NewBot calls getMe during construction; with no internet at boot the fx app fails and tgshd exits, taking health monitoring (incl. network-outage SMS alerts, FR-007/FR-008) down with it. Repro: start tgshd with network blocked. Expected: the daemon starts (telebot Settings.Offline or deferred getMe with retry), health runs from boot, Telegram sends queue until connectivity returns.

title: check --once interleaves adapter log lines (e.g. pinger WARN) with its verdict output
description: Symptom: running tgshd check --once as a normal user prints a raw zap WARN line from pkg/ping between the <VERDICT> lines (stderr interleaved in the terminal). Repro: non-root check --once with a network section. Expected: one-shot mode logs at error level only (or to a quiet logger) so the output reads as the documented line format.

title: Notifier marks an abandoned send in flight in a second lock step, so a concurrent Merge can mark the wrong ID
description: pkg/health/notify/notify.go sendTelegram/sendSMS/sendTelegramOrSMS call n.track(n.enqueue(...), err) in two separately locked steps. A Merge (first successful Load in Do) between them renumbers the new item; track then marks a stale ID that may belong to a stored message: a late success removes the wrong message and the real one is re-sent. Reachable from the /retire goroutine (runner/retire.go) racing Do's first Load. Fix: enqueue and mark in flight under one lock acquisition.

title: Health notifier sends invalid UTF-8 from check output to Telegram unchanged
description: pkg/health/notify render() does not normalise invalid UTF-8 (pkg/sms runs strings.ToValidUTF8 before escaping). A command/http check whose output contains invalid bytes yields a message Telegram rejects; the queued alert is retried until dropped after 7 days. Fix: strings.ToValidUTF8(text, "\uFFFD") before truncation/escaping; test with invalid bytes.

title: Heartbeat update drops a live planned_until on a read I/O error
description: Deferred minor ts-plm.2.10: the daemon's heartbeat update swallows any ReadHeartbeat error (including I/O errors) and rewrites without planned_until. Only a missing/corrupt file may reset it; on an I/O error keep the previous planned_until (from memory) or skip the write and report.
close_reason: fixed in final-review wave, re-review ADDRESSED

title: tlg-or-sms no longer falls back to SMS while a hung Telegram send keeps the lane busy
description: Fix-wave re-review #1 (regression from ts-plm.20). notify.go:373 treats every ErrNotSent as 'queue for Telegram, no SMS'. errChannelBusy (runner/deliver.go) only occurs while an abandoned Telegram send is still hung — a strong sign Telegram is down — so during a black-holed Telegram API later tlg-or-sms PROBLEMs never go out by SMS. Ruling: keep the SMS fallback for errChannelBusy; skip SMS only for errDeliveryDeadline (SMS lane is past the same deadline). Test both.

title: A standby excluded or never-seen drive silently suspends missing-drive detection
description: Fix-wave re-review #2. disks.go:486/506/518: byNode skips excluded serials and never tracks them, so a standby node holding an excluded drive (or a drive never read awake) is always an orphan, and any orphan suspends judgeMissing for all drives with no signal. Fix: remember the nodes of excluded drives (and attribute asleep nodes to them), and do not let an asleep orphan suspend the missing judgement indefinitely (e.g. only while unseen for less than a bound, or report a checker error once). Tests incl. the excluded-drive case.

title: Notifier truncates to 4096 runes; Telegram limits UTF-16 code units
description: Symptom: pkg/health/notify render() caps the body at 4096 runes after the host prefix. Telegram counts message length in UTF-16 code units, so emoji/astral characters (2 units each) can push a capped message over 4096 and Telegram rejects it; the queued alert is retried until dropped after 7 days. Repro: Notify a message whose text is 4000 emoji. Expected: the final text sent to Telegram is <= 4096 UTF-16 units (truncate with …), same rule as the inbox worker (T037 fix).
